const patch = "*** Begin Patch
*** Add File: _docs/frontend-flows/09-record.md
+# Flow 09 — Reference playback, microphone capture, take review and acceptance
+
+Date: 2026-10-22 (Asia/Qyzylorda).
+Status: initial specification draft; owner decisions listed under **Open decisions** are unresolved.
+Mode: specification only. No implementation, mock, visual validation or executed test is represented by this document.
+
+## 1. Purpose and authority
+
+This flow lets an authenticated project owner rehearse a prepared turn against the original scene, capture one microphone performance within that turn's fixed window, review the candidate, replace the turn's accepted take safely, and continue through the project.
+
+The [shared frontend contract](00-shared-contract.md) governs the shell, visual direction, localization, service boundary and cross-flow behavior. The latest owner choices recorded there override conflicting older wording in SPEC-001 and BR-001. In particular, the video remains visible and moving during capture; older requirements to hide it do not apply to this flow.
+
+Unchanged recording and take-safety invariants come from BR-001-R07–R16 and SPEC-001 §§4.3–4.6, AC-06 and AC-08–AC-13. This flow does not redefine preparation, final mixing, project retention or public sharing.
+
+## 2. Entry, completion and scope
+
+### Entry
+
+The user enters Record from a prepared project when:
+
+- the selected section and its current preparation revision are available;
+- at least one current turn exists;
+- the current account can access the project;
+- the turn has a valid fixed recording window, including its already-defined margins;
+- the original video/reference-audio source can be prepared for synchronized playback.
+
+The initial current turn is the explicitly requested turn when the route or prior action supplies one. The fallback turn-selection rule is **OPEN-09-06**.
+
+### Successful per-turn exit
+
+Selecting `Next` with a reviewable candidate starts acceptance. The flow may leave the current turn only after the candidate media and its authoritative association with the compatible turn revision are durably saved. A successful replacement becomes the one current accepted take for that turn.
+
+- If another turn follows under the chosen navigation rule, Record opens that turn without autoplay or automatic capture.
+- If this was the last required acceptance and every turn now has a compatible accepted take, result assembly starts automatically and the user moves to the Result progress experience.
+- If result-job creation fails after the take is durably accepted, the accepted take remains saved; recovery belongs to Flow 10 and must not roll the take back.
+
+### Other exits
+
+The user may try to move to another turn or workspace destination while an unaccepted candidate exists. That transition is guarded by the leave-candidate decision in **OPEN-09-02**. Already accepted takes remain saved regardless of the choice.
+
+### Out of scope
+
+- preparing, reprocessing, editing or adding turns (Flow 08);
+- final result mixing, rendering, playback and download (Flow 10);
+- project-list and long-term resume presentation (Flow 11);
+- a multi-take library, performance scoring, voice cloning, translation, time stretching, automatic performance fitting or microphone-gain editing;
+- device calibration, audio enhancement controls or device selection unless separately approved.
+
+## 3. Experience principles
+
+The screen's first question is: **What do I say now, and can I perform it against the scene?** The moving video is therefore the dominant and largest element. The current target line follows it in a smaller but plainly readable text block, followed by the playable audio timeline and the recording controls.
+
+This is a focused work screen inside the shared project shell, not a dashboard or landing page. It uses the shared light rehearsal-room direction:
+
+- white or light-gray working surfaces and a black video stage;
+- flat controls and quiet surface separation, without gradients, glows or decorative effects;
+- red reserved for active recording and errors;
+- no oversized hero heading, KPI cards, ornamental badges or repeated icon tiles;
+- the project identity, current workspace step and save state remain visible through the shared shell;
+- exact fonts, colors, radii, spacing, desktop proportions and control placement remain open in the shared design contract.
+
+## 4. Screen anatomy
+
+The Record screen contains the following semantic regions in reading order. Their exact desktop grid, dimensions and sticky behavior are **OPEN-09-07**.
+
+1. **Shared project shell**
+   - compact global navigation;
+   - project identity and Prepare / Record / Result workspace context;
+   - authoritative save status;
+   - no permanent sidebar.
+2. **Turn context**
+   - current turn position and enough speaker identity to distinguish the target;
+   - an indication of whether the turn has an accepted compatible take, needs a take, or has an unaccepted candidate;
+   - any direct turn navigator or previous/next affordance is unresolved under **OPEN-09-06**.
+3. **Moving video stage**
+   - the largest region on desktop and phone;
+   - displays the selected-section scene at the current turn window;
+   - remains visible and moving during original audition, candidate audition and microphone capture;
+   - plays full original audio during capture, including overlapping speakers;
+   - uses the authoritative section timeline and never extends or time-stretches it.
+4. **Target line**
+   - a small, readable line immediately below the video;
+   - shows or highlights only the current character's target during capture, including descriptive non-speech captions where the prepared turn contains them;
+   - must remain readable over the entire capture state and must not be covered by transient status or controls.
+5. **Audio timeline and common transport**
+   - a playable waveform/timeline below the target text;
+   - one common play/pause control;
+   - one `Original` / `My recording` source toggle;
+   - a visible playhead and accessible time information;
+   - source/waveform semantics, scrubbing behavior and the meaning of `My recording` while both an accepted take and an unaccepted candidate exist are unresolved under **OPEN-09-01** and **OPEN-09-05**.
+6. **Reference-audio volume**
+   - changes only the audible original/reference level for the user;
+   - never changes the captured microphone media, saved take gain or final-mix gain;
+   - remains independent from the device/system microphone input level.
+7. **Capture and review actions**
+   - ready state: `Listen` and `Record` are available when their media prerequisites are ready;
+   - capture state: `Stop` replaces the record action and the fixed-window progress is perceivable;
+   - candidate state: the user can listen, rerecord or choose `Next`;
+   - saving state: the acceptance action is pending and duplicate submissions are prevented;
+   - there is no separate mandatory Save button in the normal forward path.
+8. **Inline state and recovery message**
+   - appears next to the failed or blocked action, not as an unrelated full-screen banner;
+   - states what failed, whether the candidate or prior accepted take is safe, and the available next action;
+   - never reports a candidate as saved before durable acceptance completes.
+
+## 5. State model and transitions
+
+### 5.1 Loading the turn
+
+The screen loads the project revision, ordered turns, current turn revision, fixed capture window, accepted-take metadata, original media readiness and any eligible in-session candidate.
+
+- Keep the final layout stable while loading: stage, target-line and timeline regions retain their shape.
+- A partial load error is shown in the region that failed with a retry action.
+- Record stays unavailable until both microphone capture and reference playback can start against the same timing basis.
+- Loading must not start playback, request microphone permission or begin capture.
+
+### 5.2 Listen to the original
+
+With `Original` selected, `Listen`/play starts the video and full original audio at the turn window. It stops at the fixed window end unless the still-open timeline policy selects a different behavior. Pause and replay do not create or alter a candidate.
+
+Starting any capture stops current transport playback before the capture timing basis begins. Starting capture then plays the same turn window with its full original audio and moving video.
+
+### 5.3 Start capture
+
+`Record` has no countdown. One user activation initiates readiness and capture:
+
+1. If microphone permission or media readiness is still pending, show that pending state without counting down or pretending capture has started.
+2. After microphone and reference playback are both ready, begin capture immediately on the synchronized turn-window timing basis.
+3. Start the moving video and full original reference audio for that window.
+4. Show an unmistakable recording state, elapsed/remaining boundary information and `Stop`.
+
+The exact preflight timing, allowed start tolerance, capture-latency trimming/padding and synchronization-recovery policy remain **OPEN-09-08** and must be measured on supported desktop and phone browsers. No completed take may be fabricated when permission is denied or reference playback does not start.
+
+### 5.4 Stop and auto-stop
+
+- `Stop` ends capture early and yields a shorter candidate when usable media exists.
+- Reaching the fixed maximum window auto-stops capture.
+- Capture never extends the source window, video duration or prepared timing.
+- A shorter valid take leaves the target character silent for the unused remainder; background and other characters continue according to preview/result rules.
+- The minimum recoverable media/tolerance boundary is **OPEN-09-08**. The existence of a user-initiated early stop is not itself an error.
+
+After capture stops, remain on the same turn. Do not autoplay the candidate and do not navigate automatically.
+
+### 5.5 Candidate review
+
+The stopped media is an **unaccepted candidate** until acceptance completes. The UI must distinguish it from the durable accepted take.
+
+- The candidate can be auditioned with the video and the one common transport.
+- Review uses one processed background. Saved replacement voices play for turns that have accepted compatible takes; original voices remain for unrecorded characters, including overlaps. The candidate substitutes for its target only for its own audition.
+- Imperfect original-speaker isolation is not hidden. The user may continue after hearing it.
+- `Rerecord` starts another immediate capture for the same fixed window.
+- `Next` is the acceptance action. It does not navigate first and save later.
+
+The exact relationship among the candidate, a prior accepted take, the two-option source toggle and repeated rerecord attempts is **OPEN-09-05**. No design may expose a third saved-take library implicitly.
+
+### 5.6 Accept and continue
+
+When `Next` is selected:
+
+1. Freeze the candidate identity and its project/turn/preparation/timing revisions.
+2. Persist the media and its authoritative association idempotently.
+3. Verify that the accepted association is durable and compatible with the current turn timing.
+4. Only then replace the prior accepted take and update project progress.
+5. Navigate according to the selected next-turn policy, or start Result assembly after the last required acceptance.
+
+The prior accepted take remains authoritative through upload, validation and association commit. A failure, stale completion, duplicate response, canceled request or incompatible turn revision must not erase or replace it.
+
+Text-only or speaker-label edits preserve take compatibility. A turn timing change makes the existing take ineligible for output and rejects stale candidate acceptance; the old media remains retained until a compatible replacement is durably accepted.
+
+### 5.7 Rerecord
+
+Rerecord never deletes the prior accepted take. The treatment of an existing unaccepted candidate while the new attempt is in progress or fails is **OPEN-09-09**. Whatever policy is selected must expose at most one current candidate and must not imply a multi-take library.
+
+### 5.8 Leave with an unaccepted candidate
+
+Attempting to leave the candidate behind must open a decision rather than silently save or silently discard it. The covered destinations include any enabled turn switch, Prepare, Result, My projects, New dub and browser history navigation. Exact actions and save-failure behavior are **OPEN-09-02**.
+
+An already accepted take is not at risk in this decision. A confirmed discard affects only the unaccepted candidate. Unexpected tab/browser/process closure is governed separately by **OPEN-09-03**.
+
+## 6. Failure, interruption and recovery behavior
+
+### 6.1 Microphone permission or device failure before capture
+
+- Permission denied, no input device, device busy, unsupported capture or a readiness timeout leaves the user on the turn with no new candidate.
+- Explain the specific recoverable action where the platform exposes it: grant permission, connect/close the competing device, or retry.
+- Keep `Listen` available when original playback remains usable.
+- Preserve the prior accepted take and any already-existing candidate according to **OPEN-09-09**.
+- Do not repeatedly trigger the browser permission prompt without a new user action.
+
+### 6.2 Reference playback failure before or during capture
+
+- If the full original reference cannot start, do not start microphone capture.
+- If reference/video loses its timing basis during capture, stop the attempt and classify it through the interrupted-take rule below.
+- Never accept a take as normally synchronized merely because microphone bytes exist.
+
+### 6.3 Interrupted take
+
+Interruptions include device disconnection, audio-track end, browser background suspension, incoming-call/media interruption, navigation, page lifecycle termination and loss of the synchronized reference clock.
+
+- Stop active capture as soon as the interruption is known.
+- If actual usable media exists and the attempt satisfies the still-open compatibility/tolerance rule, expose it honestly as an interrupted candidate that may be listened to, rerecorded or accepted as a shorter take.
+- If media is missing, corrupt or outside the allowed timing contract, expose capture failure and no candidate.
+- Never manufacture recoverable media or label an interrupted candidate as accepted.
+- The prior accepted take remains authoritative throughout.
+
+The exact quality/timing threshold and which interruption classes may yield a candidate are **OPEN-09-08**.
+
+### 6.4 Candidate acceptance/save failure
+
+- Stay on the same turn.
+- State that the new recording was not saved and whether the candidate remains available in the current session.
+- Preserve the prior accepted take unchanged.
+- Allow a retry of acceptance when the same candidate remains valid, or rerecord.
+- A stale candidate caused by a timing/revision change cannot be force-saved; reload the authoritative turn and record a compatible candidate.
+- Do not advance progress, navigate or start result assembly until durable acceptance succeeds.
+
+### 6.5 Session/authentication or connectivity loss
+
+- A failed authenticated save does not turn local capture completion into a saved take.
+- Reauthentication or reconnection may retry only against the same frozen candidate and compatible turn revision.
+- Exact candidate durability through reload, sign-in round trip, crash and device transfer is **OPEN-09-03**.
+- Competing-tab acceptance requires authoritative revision fencing; a stale tab cannot overwrite a newer accepted take silently.
+
+### 6.6 Result-start failure after last acceptance
+
+The last take remains accepted. Show the Result flow's recoverable assembly-start state rather than returning the recording to candidate status or asking the user to record again.
+
+## 7. Desktop, phone and input behavior
+
+### Desktop
+
+- The video stage owns the greatest visual area.
+- The target line and playable timeline remain directly below it in that order.
+- Turn context, transport, volume and actions must fit without making the video secondary.
+- Exact columns, maximum width, side regions and whether turn navigation is adjacent to or below the stage are **OPEN-09-07**.
+
+### Phone
+
+- Use the shared compact phone navigation; no persistent sidebar.
+- Keep the same vertical priority: moving video, readable target line, playable timeline, then actions.
+- Controls must meet a minimum 44px touch target and the page must not scroll horizontally.
+- Record, Stop and the primary continuation action remain reachable while their state is active, but sticky/fixed behavior is **OPEN-09-07** because it affects video space and keyboard/safe-area handling.
+- Source switching, time reading and volume remain operable without hover.
+- Browser backgrounding during capture follows the interrupted-take contract; the product must not imply reliable background capture.
+
+### Keyboard and assistive technology
+
+- Every transport, source toggle, volume control, record/stop/rerecord/next action and turn-navigation control is keyboard operable in logical reading order.
+- Visible focus is required on the light surfaces and black stage controls.
+- Recording state, elapsed/remaining limit, stop result, candidate status, save progress and failures are announced without repeatedly interrupting the target line.
+- Recording and error states use text/icon/state semantics in addition to red.
+- The waveform has an accessible transport/time alternative; a screen reader must not traverse decorative waveform samples individually.
+- Any scrubber is an accessible slider with current time, minimum, maximum and keyboard increments. Whether scrubbing is allowed, and during which source/state, is **OPEN-09-01**.
+- Motion unrelated to user action is absent. Reduced-motion preference must not remove the visible playhead or recording-state information needed to operate the flow.
+
+## 8. Visible language and localization
+
+The interface supports English and Russian. Labels use sentence case, plain verbs and the same action name through pending, success and error feedback. Speaker names and transcript text are user/project content and must support mixed Cyrillic/Latin text without truncating the active line beyond comprehension.
+
+Confirmed action concepts are `Listen`, `Record`, `Stop`, `Rerecord`, `Next`, `Original` and `My recording`. Exact English/Russian copy, permission guidance, interruption wording, destructive leave wording and save-error messages are **OPEN-09-10**. Working translations must not be treated as approved copy until that decision is resolved.
+
+Messages must communicate these facts explicitly when applicable:
+
+- microphone permission or device readiness is blocking capture;
+- recording begins immediately when ready;
+- the maximum window was reached or the user stopped early;
+- a candidate is not yet saved;
+- a previous accepted take remains safe;
+- the new take is saving, saved, or failed to save;
+- leaving will affect only the unaccepted candidate;
+- an interrupted take is recoverable or was not captured.
+
+## 9. Logical service contract
+
+The frontend talks through the centralized interchangeable services boundary. Names below identify responsibilities, not transport endpoints or implementation modules.
+
+### Load recording context
+
+**Input:** account/session context, project ID, optional requested turn ID.
+
+**Result:** authorized project summary; preparation revision; ordered turns; each turn's ID, speaker/text, source start/end and margins, timing revision and accepted-take eligibility/status; project completion state; original video/reference descriptors; save status.
+
+**Errors:** unauthorized/not found, preparation unavailable/stale, invalid turn window, media unavailable, temporary service failure.
+
+### Prepare synchronized reference playback
+
+**Input:** project/preparation/turn revision, fixed source window, requested playback source.
+
+**Result:** playable media handles and a shared timing basis ready for explicit user playback or capture.
+
+**Errors:** original/reference unavailable, unsupported media, readiness timeout, stale revision. Readiness must be distinguished from playback actually starting.
+
+### Capture candidate
+
+**Input:** frozen project/turn/timing revision and maximum local duration derived from the fixed source window.
+
+**Events/result:** permission/readiness state; capture started timestamp/timing basis; progress; user stop, automatic stop or interruption reason; actual media metadata; recoverability/compatibility evidence. Capture completion alone is not persistence.
+
+**Errors:** permission denied, no/busy/lost device, unsupported capture, no media, encoding failure, reference synchronization loss.
+
+### Audition source
+
+**Input:** source selection, current turn window, accepted-take map, optional candidate identity and current revisions.
+
+**Result:** synchronized video plus the preview mix: one processed background, accepted replacement voices where available, original voices for unrecorded characters, and candidate substitution only for candidate review.
+
+**Errors:** source unavailable, candidate expired, stale/incompatible take, preview isolation unavailable. The result must not claim perfect separation.
+
+### Accept candidate
+
+**Input:** project ID; turn ID; preparation and timing revisions; immutable candidate identity/media; duration/timing metadata; idempotency identity; expected current accepted-take revision.
+
+**Success:** durable accepted-take identity and revision, replaced-take outcome, authoritative turn/project progress, whether all turns are now complete, and next eligible turn under the resolved navigation rule.
+
+**Errors:** upload/validation/storage/association failure, stale preparation/timing/accepted-take revision, incompatible or missing media, unauthorized session, connectivity failure. Errors must state whether retry with the same candidate is possible.
+
+### Start result assembly
+
+**Input:** project ID and authoritative all-turns-complete revision returned after the final acceptance.
+
+**Success:** result job identity and Result-flow state.
+
+**Errors:** incomplete/stale revision, job creation failure, service unavailable. This operation must be idempotent and must not undo the final accepted take.
+
+### Resolve candidate on leave
+
+This is a flow-level composition of `Accept candidate`, discard-local-candidate behavior and navigation. It must follow **OPEN-09-02** and **OPEN-09-03**; discard must never delete the accepted take.
+
+## 10. Persistence, ownership and concurrency
+
+- One durable current accepted take exists per turn; temporary artifacts do not form a take library.
+- A candidate is not durable merely because capture stopped, local playback works or an upload progress indicator completed.
+- The prior accepted take stays authoritative until the compatible replacement association commits successfully.
+- Accepted takes belong to the account-owned project and restore through normal project resume.
+- A late response for an older candidate, timing revision or accepted-take revision cannot replace newer work.
+- Timing edits invalidate output eligibility; text/speaker-only edits preserve it.
+- The exact storage/lifetime of unaccepted candidates is **OPEN-09-03**. Superseded artifact cleanup is a backend retention concern and cannot be inferred from the visible one-take model.
+- The flow must expose enough authoritative state to distinguish `candidate`, `saving`, `accepted`, `failed` and `stale`; optimistic UI may not collapse them into one saved checkmark.
+
+## 11. Acceptance criteria
+
+All criteria are unexecuted. Criteria marked **BLOCKED** cannot pass until the named open decision is resolved.
+
+- [ ] **F09-AC-01 — Visual hierarchy:** On desktop and phone, the moving video is the largest element; target line and playable timeline appear below it in that order, and capture never hides or freezes the stage intentionally.
+- [ ] **F09-AC-02 — Immediate bounded capture:** One `Record` activation starts capture immediately after real microphone/reference readiness, with no countdown; full original audio and moving video play, early Stop yields an eligible shorter take when valid, and the fixed maximum auto-stops without extending or stretching the source.
+- [ ] **F09-AC-03 — Independent volume:** Changing reference volume changes only local original/reference playback and never captured microphone media, saved-take gain or final-mix gain.
+- [ ] **F09-AC-04 — No implicit continuation:** Capture completion stays on the current turn with no autoplay, auto-save-as-accepted or navigation. The candidate can be listened to, rerecorded or accepted with `Next`.
+- [ ] **F09-AC-05 — One transport:** Original and My recording use one common playback control and a two-option source toggle. **BLOCKED by OPEN-09-01 and OPEN-09-05** for waveform/source resolution details.
+- [ ] **F09-AC-06 — Honest candidate:** An unaccepted or interrupted candidate is visibly distinct from the durable accepted take; missing/corrupt media is never represented as recoverable or saved.
+- [ ] **F09-AC-07 — Safe replacement:** Capture, upload, validation, stale response or association failure leaves the prior accepted take authoritative. Only a durable compatible commit replaces it.
+- [ ] **F09-AC-08 — Acceptance before navigation:** `Next` persists idempotently before moving. A failed save stays on the turn, starts no Result job and reports whether the same candidate can be retried.
+- [ ] **F09-AC-09 — Last turn:** Final durable acceptance updates project completion and automatically starts Result assembly; a result-start failure preserves all accepted takes and enters Flow 10 recovery.
+- [ ] **F09-AC-10 — Preview mix:** Candidate review uses one processed background, accepted voices for recorded turns and original voices for unrecorded turns; overlapping original speakers remain audible where not yet replaced, and imperfect isolation can be auditioned and accepted.
+- [ ] **F09-AC-11 — Revision safety:** Timing changes reject/invalidate stale candidates and require a replacement; text/speaker-only edits retain take eligibility; competing-tab or duplicate completions cannot silently overwrite newer accepted work.
+- [ ] **F09-AC-12 — Leave guard:** Leaving with an unaccepted candidate follows an explicit save/discard/stay policy without risking accepted takes. **BLOCKED by OPEN-09-02**.
+- [ ] **F09-AC-13 — Unexpected close:** Reload/crash/close behavior represents candidate durability truthfully and restores accepted takes. **BLOCKED by OPEN-09-03**.
+- [ ] **F09-AC-14 — Rerecord safety:** Rerecord never deletes the prior accepted take and obeys the one-candidate rule. **BLOCKED by OPEN-09-09** for candidate replacement on failed rerecord.
+- [ ] **F09-AC-15 — Permission and interruption:** Permission denial, missing/busy/lost device, blocked reference playback and background suspension produce specific recoverable states; no false take is created. **BLOCKED by OPEN-09-08** for measurable compatibility thresholds.
+- [ ] **F09-AC-16 — Responsive operation:** All core operations work at the target desktop/tablet/phone widths without horizontal page scrolling, hidden target text or inaccessible active controls. **BLOCKED by OPEN-09-07** for exact composition/sticky policy.
+- [ ] **F09-AC-17 — Accessibility:** Keyboard and screen-reader users can identify source, time, capture state, candidate/save state and errors; focus is visible; red is not the sole cue; waveform graphics have an operable semantic alternative.
+- [ ] **F09-AC-18 — Localization:** English and Russian preserve action meaning and critical save/interruption facts without clipping the active target or controls. **BLOCKED by OPEN-09-10** for approved copy.
+
+## 12. Verification plan
+
+This is a proposed test plan, not evidence of execution.
+
+### Contract and state tests
+
+- reducer/store transitions for loading, ready, original playback, capture, early stop, auto-stop, candidate, rerecord, saving, accepted, save failed, stale and interrupted states;
+- ensure no candidate or accepted state is synthesized from permission/reference failure;
+- ensure `Next` is idempotent and navigation/result-start waits for durable acceptance;
+- ensure an old accepted take survives every candidate/capture/save failure path;
+- revision-fence tests for timing edits, text/speaker edits, competing tabs, duplicate callbacks and out-of-order completion;
+- final-turn acceptance followed by successful and failed result-job creation.
+
+### Media/timing integration tests
+
+- supported desktop and phone browsers with granted, prompt, denied and revoked microphone permission;
+- full-window auto-stop and multiple user early-stop durations, including the shortest allowed boundary once **OPEN-09-08** is resolved;
+- video/reference/capture start alignment and measured tolerance under normal and throttled conditions;
+- reference playback rejection, device loss, Bluetooth/device change, tab backgrounding and phone media interruption;
+- overlapping-speaker preview with saved/unsaved combinations and one background;
+- candidate and accepted-take playback after upload/reload according to **OPEN-09-03**.
+
+### Interaction and responsive tests
+
+- desktop, tablet and phone layouts using long English, long Russian and mixed-script target lines;
+- portrait and landscape source video while preserving video dominance and reachable controls;
+- keyboard-only operation, focus order, focus restoration after dialogs/errors and no conflicting shortcuts while typing/using sliders;
+- screen-reader announcements for record start/stop, candidate ready, saving, accepted and failed states;
+- 200% zoom/reflow, high-contrast/forced-colors where supported, reduced motion and touch-only operation;
+- leave attempts through every enabled internal destination and browser history after **OPEN-09-02** is resolved.
+
+### Failure evidence
+
+For each case record environment/browser/device, project and turn revision, command or manual procedure, observed timestamps/durations, expected and actual authoritative take, result, date and evidence location. Physical-device and acoustic findings must be separated from mock/service-contract results.
+
